answers.question: Q1
answers.correction:
The identification statements and their strengths are quoted and graded correctly. Four of the six texts state the identification; the other two, 2203.17137 and 2303.15645, have 0 matches for 'dark' (verifier's count). Two overstatements:
- 'In every case the dark field φ̃ ... is the background of a dual momentum p̃' holds only for 2407.06207 §3.3 and 2604.19418 §5.1. Minic 2023 makes no field-level statement at all. 2610.19522 §3.2 states that φ̃ does not commute with φ, but not the p̃-background.
- 'The latest text is the most hedged' is a judgment. Minic 2023's 'natural candidates for dark matter' is as hedged as 2610.19522's 'a candidate for the invisible matter sector'.
The answer also omits a restatement in 2604.19418 §5.2 (below).
counter_evidence: 2305.12593 §2: 'metaparticles (correlated objects of visible particles and their duals, which, in turn, represent natural candidates for dark matter [10])'. No dual field and no p̃-background appear in the paper.
2610.19522 §3.2: 'it is a candidate for the invisible matter sector (dual to the observed, visible, Standard Model sector)'. Non-commutation is stated; the p̃-background is not.

2604.19418 §5.2: 'At the same time, metastring has the relevant structure to reproduce the SM degrees of freedom and their dual, “dark” counterparts, as well as naturally small vacuum energy.' (lit.py: FOUND)

answers.question: Q2
answers.correction:
Right that x̃ is used both for a rescaled momentum on one phase space and for an independent coordinate of a doubled phase space. The verifier derived the doubling independently from the paper's Lagrangian (rank 4; brackets_v.out). Four corrections:
(1) The answer never gives the papers' own string-theoretic definition of x̃. They build it from left- and right-movers, x = x_L + x_R and x̃ = x̃_L − x̃_R (2407.06207 eq. 3.11; 2604.19418 eq. 5.10; 2610.19522 eq. 3.7). That is the closed string's T-dual coordinate, which the papers tie to double field theory. Its quasi-period is the string momentum, or 'the winding number in the usual treatment of T-duality on compact spaces' (2610.19522 §3.2). The brief asks for exactly this when x̃ is a winding-type coordinate.
(2) 2610.19522's derivation belongs to use (b), not (a). Its X̃ = Y 'lives in momentum space' because ∂_σY = P, the momentum density. But [X, X̃] = 2πiλ² (λ² ~ α′), and X̃ has its own conjugate Π̃ at ħ (eq. 3.11). So it is not the canonical conjugate of x on one phase space at ħ.
(3) 'Nothing separating the two uses' understates what the authors do: they explicitly identify the two uses. 2407.06207 §3.2 says the x̃ ≡ p/ε description 'will appear in what follows in the metastring formulation'. The modular field φ_λ(x, x̃) is obtained by second-quantizing the Zak-transformed wave function (2407.06207 §3.3; 2604.19418 §5.1). A transition sentence marks the step from 'covariant quantum phase space' to 'modular spacetime'. What is missing is any statement that x̃ changes status.
(4) The answer's list of scales omits one: 2407.06207 §5.1 assumes the dual phase space is of Planck size, with l̃ = ℓ_s²/√(l_Λ l_P).
A note for the reader's executed check: the single phase space alone also gives [X, X̃] = iλ² in dimensionful form (X = q, X̃ = λ²p/ħ; brackets_v.out). It is [x, p] = iħ = [x̃, p̃] with [p, p̃] = 0 that forces the doubling, not the [x, x̃] commutator.

answers.question: Q4
answers.correction:
The three 'layers' and the quotes are right, and the decoupling statement does occur only in 2407.06207 (verifier's greps of 2604.19418, 2610.19522 and 2307.16712 v2). Three corrections:
(1) The layers are one structure in the school's own derivation. LHEP 2021, which 2407.06207 cites for the Berry-phase-like term, derives the λ²[[A, Ã]] mixing from the same λ²p·(dp̃/dτ) term that makes x and x̃ non-commute, by the minimal-coupling shift p → p + A, p̃ → p̃ + Ã. After integrating over x̃ it becomes −(λ⁸/L¹⁰) f[[A, Ã]]. Eq. 3.8 omits it because it is written 'to leading order in λ'.
(2) 2407.06207 §5.3 first gives M_SM as a 'would-be unification scale ... ∼10^{15-16} GeV' and then as 4.5×10^14 GeV; the decoupling identification uses the latter. The verifier recomputed 4.484×10^14 GeV from Table 1's definition with M_Λ = 1.1×10⁻³ eV. This value also reproduces Table 1's m_ν3 = 3.5×10⁻² eV (msm_v.out).
(3) The cited source does not support a gravity-only reading at low energy. LHEP 2021 calls the correlation invisible in effective field theory, vanishing as λ → 0 or L → ∞. But it also says the dual photon's correlation is 'finite even in the limit of zero momenta (deep infrared)' and may show up as 'correlated events in the accelerators'. 'Below ~10^14 GeV the 2024 restatement has gravity-only interaction, as under #11's strict P4' is therefore accurate for one sentence of one paper, not for the school's account of the term, which the 2024 paper leaves unreconciled.

answers.question: Q9
answers.correction:
Confirmed that no potential, order parameter or spontaneous breaking is given. 'spontan' occurs only as 'spontaneous emission' and in the Coleman–Weinberg title; 'order parameter' occurs once, for a finite-temperature Landau–Ginzburg field in 2407.06207 §2.3. Three omissions:
(1) The papers contain #11 P2′'s own formula. 2610.19522 §3.2 defines J = η⁻¹H, so η = HJ, and calls (η, J) 'a chiral structure' after FLM 2014 [63], arXiv:1307.7080. It also writes 'η = ωK, with K² = 1, so K is the real structure'. No choice of J or K is called spontaneous.
(2) 'Not as a mirror vacuum' is the reader's inference. The papers do put the two halves on a par, though neither is called a vacuum: 'spacetime and momentum space appear on equal footing as slices of phase space' (2407.06207 §3); modular QFT has 'both spacetime and dual spacetime as natural limits' (§3.1).
(3) Further accounts of why spacetime is selected are missing:
- spacetime 'only appears through decoupling, in the large scale limit' (2305.12593 §2);
- 'due to gravity’s extreme weakness, only classical spacetime metric is observed at low energies and long distances' (2610.19522 §3.2);
- averaging over x̃ gives classical evolution in the spacetime basis (2604.19418 §5.1; 2610.19522 §3.2 and §4.1).

record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3, 'What differs': 'All three judges for C1 read this as predicting couplings between dark and visible matter beyond gravity' and 'The scope judge answers that the school still expects a detection, through the entanglement, and states no permanent null.' Also findings.json, C1 findings for 2407.06207 and 2604.19418, difference (2): 'correlated/entangled with visible matter through non-gravitational terms ... the school expects it to be detectable.'
record_contradictions.note:
The source text is verified. 2407.06207 §5.3 puts the Berry-phase-like mixing above a decoupling energy M_SM ≃ 4.5×10^14 GeV, below which dark and visible matter 'interact as required, only gravitationally'. The verifier recomputed 4.484×10^14 GeV; the same paragraph also calls M_SM a 'would-be unification scale ... ∼10^{15-16} GeV'. The statement is absent from 2604.19418, 2610.19522 and 2307.16712 v2 (verifier's greps).
This validly qualifies findings.json's difference (2) as applied to 2407.06207. In that paper the non-gravitational term sits above M_SM, and the only dark-sector observable named is astrophysical (a₀).
It does not refute the note's account of the 2020–2021 papers. LHEP 2021, which 2407.06207 cites for this very term, says the dual photon's correlation 'is finite even in the limit of zero momenta (deep infrared)' and that such correlations 'might be found in correlated events in the accelerators'. It also says the correlation 'becomes invisible in effective field theory' (all FOUND in 2010.15610).
The school's papers disagree with one another on low-energy coupling, and the record should state both positions.

record_contradictions.record_says: wiki/summary.md line 34: 'Its core is published (Minic and coauthors, 2020), their sector correlated with ours; neither form was found.' review/wiki-build-flags.md item 64: 'Their dual sector is correlated with ours; #11's couples by gravity alone under strict P4 (row 7)'. Root CLAUDE.md, 2026-11-02 entry, has the same contrast.
record_contradictions.note:
The qualification is real and the record lacks it: one 2024 restatement (Hübsch and Minic 2024, §5.3) has gravity-only interaction below M_SM. But the contrast is not refuted, for three reasons.
(1) 'Correlated' is the school's own word, used in these same papers for a relation it claims at galactic scales: 'visible and dark matter degrees of freedom are correlated (via the minimal length λ)' (2407.06207 §3.4; 2604.19418 §5.1). 2604.19418 §5.1 calls the observed a₀ 'evidence for ... the correlation of dual fields of fuzzy dark matter to the observed Standard Model fields'.
(2) The source of the mixing term, LHEP 2021, keeps a correlation in the deep infrared and at accelerators.
(3) 2407.06207 §5.4 itself lets the dual SM contribute CP-violating phases to visible mixing.
The summary's wording is faithful to the school. What it lacks is the 2024 decoupling sentence, and the fact that the school's papers do not agree on whether low-energy coupling is gravitational only.

overall: The reader's quotations can be relied on. All 103 statement quotations and 7 auxiliary ones were found by lit.py's checker, or in a fresh download of the journal PDF; the shared cache for 2407.06207 matched a fresh arXiv fetch byte for byte; dates and venues check out (one slip: INSPIRE types 2407.06207 as 'article', with a conference record attached); and both executed checks reproduce (rank 4, derived here from the paper's own Lagrangian; M_SM = 4.484×10^14 GeV). The readings hold for identification, field content, dynamics, monopoles, dark energy and priority, but need correction in two places. On what x̃ is, the reader omits the papers' own definition of x̃ as the closed string's T-dual coordinate x_L − x_R, files 2610.19522's derivation under 'one phase space at ħ', and says nothing separates two uses that the authors explicitly identify. On coupling, the reader treats the 2024 decoupling sentence as settling the question, while LHEP 2021, which that paper cites for the same term, places the correlation in the deep infrared and at accelerators. The record contradictions are valid qualifications, not refutations: the record should add the 2024 decoupling scale and the school's internal disagreement, but 'correlated' remains the school's own claim.
